title: Efficient Bi-Level Optimization for Recommendation Denoising

problem.claim: Explicit user feedback is difficult to acquire, while implicit feedback is noisy and can undermine recommendation quality.

gap.claim: Existing implicit-feedback weighting methods calculate weights without accounting for previous iterations and often depend on prior knowledge that may be unavailable or not universally applicable.

narrative_sequence.summary: Real-world recommender systems often struggle to obtain explicit user feedback because it requires active user involvement.
Implicit feedback generated during browsing is used as a substitute for explicit feedback.
Implicit feedback contains substantial noise that reduces recommendation quality.
Prior weighting methods do not account for inter-iteration influence and may require unavailable or non-general prior knowledge.

unknowns: The proposed method is not described.
